epics.name: Get an invoice paid
epics.intent: Steps: Create an invoice, Send it, Chase an unpaid one, See what is owed.

epics.name: Set up the account
epics.intent: Steps: Add the business details, Connect a bank account.

stories.name: Add the business details

job.when: I have signed up and nothing is filled in yet
job.want: add the business details that appear on an invoice
job.so: an invoice I send looks like it came from a real business

stories.body: Name, address, tax number and logo. These appear on every invoice, so an invoice cannot be sent before this exists. The brief does not say which fields are legally required and that varies by country — see the spike.

criteria.text: the form states which fields appear on the invoice and which are for our records only
leaving it half-finished and coming back does not lose what was typed
every field has a label a screen reader can read

stories.name: Connect a bank account

job.want: connect the account the money should arrive in

stories.body: The brief assumes one bank account per business and never says so. Flagged rather than designed around.

criteria.text: a failed connection says what is still true — no money has moved, nothing was saved
the account number is never shown in full after it is saved

stories.name: Create an invoice

job.when: I have done work for somebody and want the money
job.so: there is a document the client can pay against

stories.body: Line items, a total, a due date and a client. What it must never do: send anything. Creating and sending are separate on purpose, because a half-written invoice reaching a client cannot be taken back.

criteria.text: nothing leaves the system from this screen — sending is a separate, deliberate action
the total is recomputed from the line items and is never typed by hand
an invoice with no line items cannot be saved as ready to send
nothing falls off the frame at any supported width

stories.name: Send an invoice

job.when: an invoice is finished and I have checked it
job.so: the client has it and the clock starts

stories.body: Sending is irreversible from the client's side. The screen exists mostly to carry that one sentence, and to show exactly what will be sent and to whom before it goes.

criteria.text: the client's email address is shown in full, next to the confirm action
a send that fails says whether the client received it or not — never 'something went wrong'
a sent invoice can be viewed but not edited

stories.name: Chase an unpaid invoice

job.when: an invoice has gone past its due date
job.want: remind the client without writing the email myself

stories.body: The brief asks for this in one line and describes nothing. Nothing is designed for it yet.

criteria.text: something serves this step — a screen exists and is reachable
a reminder says which invoice, for how much, and how overdue

stories.name: See what is owed

job.when: I want to know where I stand
job.want: see every unpaid invoice and what it adds up to
job.so: I know whether to chase anybody this week

stories.body: The one screen most people open daily. With six invoices it is a list; with six hundred it is unusable, so the density budget matters here more than anywhere else.

criteria.text: the outstanding total is visible without scrolling
overdue is distinguishable without relying on colour alone
the list stays usable at the real number of invoices, not the demo number

spikes.name: Decide: which business fields are legally required, and where
spikes.question: Which business details are legally required on an invoice, and does that vary by the country we launch in?
spikes.context: The brief lists fields without saying which are mandatory. Getting this wrong makes every invoice sent from the product legally defective, and it is not fixable after the fact.

options.label: One superset of fields, all required
options.buys: one form, one validation rule, launch anywhere
options.costs: asks every user for things most of them do not need

options.label: Per-country field sets
options.buys: each user is asked only for what applies to them
options.costs: a rule set per country, maintained forever
options.kills: launching in a new country without legal review

spikes.right_if: The superset wins if the first release is one country and the second is not imminent.
